## Why visit

An unusually complete pub experience: distinctive old rooms, local cask beer and a credible lunch stop close to the market. The curved glazed bar, tiled lobby and tiny snug make the interior worth exploring slowly. The snug is reached through the bar; ask staff rather than walking into their working space. This is a particularly good introduction to the relationship between Stockport and Robinsons, with Robinsons’ historic brewery site nearby and its beers central to the offer. Make it a meal anchor on a Stockport day, then contrast its traditional brewery-house character with Petersgate Tap or the Magnet.

## Beer

Robinsons hand-pulled ales; the brewery and CAMRA both document the cask offer. Ask about seasonal beers rather than expecting a specific November line-up. CAMRA lists Robinsons Unicorn and Dizzy Blonde among the regular brewery casks. Old Tom is seasonal and not guaranteed after its 7 November launch.

## Food

Home-cooked lunches and Sunday roasts are advertised by Robinsons. Evening kitchen service is more limited than pub opening.

## Plan the visit

Check kitchen hours and reserve if the meal is important. Heritage rooms are small; inspect the snug with staff permission.

**Getting there:** Walk from Stockport station through the town centre to Millgate.

Check [November transport issues](../logistics.md) for date-specific disruption.
